items.text: Tens are the easiest numbers to add, so spot the pairs that make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5. This frame has room for 10 dots: 7 dots and 3 gaps make 10.

items.prompt: How many more dots would fill the frame?
Tap two numbers that make 10. Clear the lot.
items.explain: 3 and 7, 8 and 2, 6 and 4. Ten every time.

items.text: The + sign means add: put the two together. 6 needs 4 to make 10, so take 4 from the 7, leaving 3. 10 and 3 is 13. To answer, tap the digits in order: 1, then 3.

items.prompt: Give 2 of the 7 to the 8 to make 10. Then add what is left.
Make 10 first, then add the rest.

items.text: A number line runs from one end number to the other in equal hops. This one goes 0 to 20 in 10 hops, so each hop is 2. Other lines are cut differently, so check first. Drag the marker; letting go answers.

items.prompt: Where does it land? Drag the marker and let go.

items.text: Bigger numbers work the same way. Hop to the next ten first: 38 needs 2 to reach 40, so split the 5 into 2 and 3. 40 and 3 is 43.

items.prompt: Hop to 40 first, then the rest.

items.text: Pairs can make 100 too. 4 and 6 make 10, so 40 and 60 make 100. With ones: 35 needs 5 to reach 40, then 60 more, so 35 and 65 make 100.
The - sign means take away. Hop down the same way: 43 is 3 above 40, so split the 5 into 3 and 2. 40 take away 2 is 38.

items.prompt: Taking away works too: hop down to 60 first.

items.text: The × sign means times: 3 × 4 is three lots of 4, so 4 + 4 + 4, which is 12. Doubling is times 2: 6 doubled is 6 + 6, which is 12.
To times by 4, double twice. 25 doubled is 50, and doubled again is 100.
43 is 4 tens and 3 ones: 40 and 3. To double it, double each part. 40 doubled is 80, 3 doubled is 6, and 80 and 6 is 86.

items.prompt: Double it: the tens, then the ones.

items.text: The ÷ sign means share equally: 86 ÷ 2 is 86 shared between 2. That is halving, the other way from doubling. Half of 80 is 40, half of 6 is 3: 43.

items.prompt: Halve it: the tens, then the ones.
items.explain: Half of 60 is 30 and half of 4 is 2: 32.

items.text: Halve one number and double the other, and the answer stays the same. 6 × 5 is 3 × 10: both are 30. So pick whichever is easier to work out.

items.prompt: Halve one number, double the other. Which has the same answer?
items.explain: Half of 16 is 8 and double 5 is 10. 8 × 10 is 80, an easy one.

items.text: An array is dots in equal rows. Here are 3 rows of 4: that is 3 × 4, and 4 + 4 + 4 is 12. Turn it on its side and it is 4 rows of 3, still 12. Either order, same answer.

items.prompt: How many dots? Count the rows, not every dot.

items.explain: Turn 4 rows of 3 on its side: 3 rows of 4. Both are 12.

items.prompt: Match each sum to its answer.

items.text: Times 10 moves every digit up a place, so 7 becomes 70 and 23 becomes 230. Times 5 is half of times 10: 7 × 10 is 70, so 7 × 5 is 35. And times 2 is doubling.

items.prompt: Move every digit up a place.

items.explain: 8 × 10 is 80, and half of that is 40.

items.prompt: Count in 5s. Where does it land?

items.explain: 14 × 10 is 140, and half of that is 70.

items.text: Times 4 is double, then double again. Times 8 is one more double. So 7 × 8 goes 7, 14, 28, 56.
Times 9 is times 10, take away one lot. 7 × 10 is 70, take away 7: 63.
Sharing is dividing. Share 8 dots into 2 equal rows and each row gets 4: 8 ÷ 2 is 4. Halving is sharing between 2.

items.prompt: 12 dots shared into 3 equal rows. How many in each row?
Halve it: the tens, then the ones.
items.explain: Half of 60 is 30 and half of 8 is 4: 34.

items.text: To share by 4, halve and halve again. Half of 48 is 24, and half of 24 is 12, so 48 ÷ 4 is 12.
Dividing by 10 is times 10 backwards: every digit moves down a place, so 70 becomes 7 and 350 becomes 35. To divide by 5, double first, then divide by 10. 35 ÷ 5: 70 ÷ 10 is 7.

items.prompt: Move every digit down a place.

items.text: Some numbers don't share evenly. Share these 7 dots between 2 people: 3 each, and 1 is left over. What is left over is called the remainder.

items.prompt: Share these between 2 people. How many are left over?
items.explain: 4 each uses 8 dots, so 1 is left over.

items.prompt: How many are left over? Three 5s is 15.
40 eggs go in boxes of 6. How many eggs are left over?
items.explain: 6 boxes of 6 is 36, and 40 take away 36 leaves 4.

items.prompt: How many are left over? Five 4s is 20.

items.text: Rounding swaps a number for a nearby one that is easy to work with. 47 sits between 40 and 50: 3 hops from 50 and 7 from 40, so 47 to the nearest 10 is 50. Exactly halfway, like 45, rounds up.

items.explain: 85 is halfway, and halfway rounds up: 90.

items.text: To the nearest 100, look at the tens. 349 has 4 tens, short of halfway to 400, so it rounds to 300. With 5 tens or more, like 350, it rounds up to 400.

items.explain: 650 has 5 tens, halfway, so it rounds up: 700.

items.text: Before you trust a total, round each number and add those. 38 + 41 is about 40 + 40, so about 80. An answer of 79 looks right; 179 is a slip somewhere.

items.sum: 38 to the nearest 10 + 43 to the nearest 10
items.prompt: Round each to the nearest 10. About how much?
Which total is about right? Round first.
Which is about right? Round first.

items.text: Per cent means out of 100, and % is its sign. This grid has 10 rows of 10, so 100 squares, and 25 are shaded: that is 25%.

items.explain: 4 full rows of 10 is 40 squares out of 100: 40%.

items.prompt: Drag the marker to 50% and let go.

items.text: A fraction is a share, written with a /. 1/2 means 1 out of 2 equal parts: a half. 1/4 is 1 out of 4, a quarter. 1/10 is 1 out of 10, a tenth.

items.explain: Four 25s make 100, so 25% is a quarter.
75% is three quarters of the way along.

items.text: 10% of 80 means a 10% share of 80. 10% is a tenth: take a 0 off, so 10% of 80 is 8. And 50% is a half.

items.explain: 10% of 30 is 3, and double that is 6.
10% of 200 is 20, and half of that is 10.

items.text: A tip is extra money you add to a bill. A 15% tip is 10%, plus half of that. On a $40 bill: 4, plus 2, is $6.

items.prompt: What is the tip? 10%, plus half of that.
items.explain: 10% is 6 and half of that is 3: $9.

items.text: Off means taken away from the price. 10% of $50 is $5, so you pay $50 take away $5: $45. And 25% is a quarter: halve, then halve again.

items.prompt: What do you pay? 25% is a quarter.
items.explain: A quarter of 80 is 20 off, so you pay $60.

items.prompt: Match each percent to its fraction.
items.explain: 50% is a half, 25% a quarter, 10% a tenth.

items.text: A fraction is part of a whole. In 1/4, the number after the / is how many equal parts there are; the number before it is how many are shaded. One of four parts is 1/4.

items.prompt: Build the fraction that is shaded.

items.text: These bars are shaded the same amount. 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 are one amount with three names.

items.explain: 2 of 4 parts is half the bar: 1/2.

items.text: Cut every part of this 1/4 into 3 pieces and you get 3/12: the same amount. Times both numbers by the same thing and the amount stays put.

items.prompt: Match the fractions that are the same amount.

items.text: These bars are the same length, so you can compare them by eye. Fewer parts means bigger parts: 1/2 is bigger than 1/8. And the further the shading reaches, the more it is.

items.explain: Fewer parts means bigger parts: a third is bigger than a quarter or a fifth.

items.prompt: Which is biggest? Look at the bars.

items.text: Fractions sit between whole numbers. Cut the gap from 0 to 1 into 4 equal hops, and each hop is 1/4. So the hops land on 1/4, 2/4, 3/4.

items.prompt: This line is cut in thirds. Drag to 2/3.

items.text: The first number can be the bigger one. Here each hop is 1/3. Three hops is 3/3, and that lands on 1: when both numbers match, it is one whole. One hop more is 4/3, past 1.

items.explain: Three halves is one whole and a half more.
Four quarters make a whole: 4/4 is 1.

items.text: A decimal point splits a whole from its parts. Call this grid 1 whole. Each row is a tenth, 0.1, and each square a hundredth, 0.01. 3 rows are shaded: 0.3.

items.prompt: What decimal is shaded? Each square is 0.01.
This line runs from 0 to 0.1. Drag to 0.04.
items.explain: Each hop is 0.01, so four hops: 0.04.

items.prompt: Match each decimal to the same amount.

items.text: Add the dollars, then the cents. $2 + $1 is $3. 50c + 75c is 125c, which is $1.25. So $4.25 altogether. Tap the point like a digit.
Change is what you get back. Count up from the price: 5c takes $6.35 to $6.40, 60c more to $7, then $3 to $10. 5c + 60c + $3 is $3.65.
A ratio says how much goes with how much. One egg makes 4 pikelets: each row here is one egg's 4. Three eggs, three rows: 12 pikelets. To scale a recipe, times every amount by the same number.

items.prompt: A cup of flour makes 3 scones: one row each. How many scones from 4 cups?
Mix 1 cup of cordial with 4 cups of water. For 3 cups of cordial, how many cups of water?
items.explain: 4 cups of water for every cup of cordial: 3 × 4 is 12.

items.prompt: Pasta for 8 people instead: how many grams?
items.explain: 8 people is twice 4, so twice 300 g: 600 g.
6 muffins is half of 12, so half the eggs: 3.

items.text: To compare packs, work out the price for one. Share the price between them: 4 for $12 is $12 ÷ 4, so $3 each.

items.prompt: Divide by 10: every digit moves down a place.

items.text: Which is the better buy? Find the price for one in each. 3 for $6 is $2 each. 5 for $9 is $1.80 each. $1.80 is less, so the 5-pack is cheaper each.

items.prompt: Which is the better buy? Compare the price for one.
items.explain: 3 for $6 is $2 each and 5 for $9 is $1.80 each: 5 for $9.

items.prompt: Match each pack to its price for one.
items.explain: 2 for $6 is $3 each, 5 for $10 is $2 each, 4 for $2 is $0.50 each.

items.prompt: Three packs now. Which is cheaper each?
items.explain: 2 for $5 is $2.50 each, 4 for $8 is $2 each, 6 for $15 is $2.50 each: 4 for $8.

items.text: Numbers keep going below zero. A - in front means below: -3 is 3 below zero. On a cold morning it can be -3 °C, and -8 °C is colder still: the further below zero, the smaller the number.

items.explain: -8 °C is furthest below zero, so it is the coldest.
-1 °C is closest to zero, so it is the warmest.

items.prompt: Level -2 is two floors under the ground floor, 0. Drag the lift there.

items.text: Cross zero in two hops. It is 3 °C and drops 5 degrees: 3 down to 0, then 2 more, so 3 - 5 is -2. Going up works the same way: -4 + 6 is 4 up to 0, then 2 more: 2.

items.prompt: It is 4 °C and drops 7 degrees. Drag to the new temperature.
A lift at level -3 goes up 5 floors. Which level?
items.explain: 3 up to the ground floor, then 2 more: level 2.

items.prompt: A lift at level 2 goes down 6 floors. Which level?
It is -6 °C at dawn and warms up 9 degrees. Drag to the new temperature.

items.text: Owing money is like being below zero. Owe $20 and you are at -20. Get $50: $20 pays what you owe, and $30 is yours. So -20 + 50 is 30.

items.prompt: You owe $30, then get paid $45. How much is yours?
items.explain: $30 pays what you owe, and $15 is yours.

items.prompt: You have $15 and spend $40 on a card. Where are you now?
items.explain: $15 takes you to 0, and you owe $25 more: -25.

items.prompt: Owe $8, then pay back $5. Drag to where you are.
items.explain: $5 of the $8 is paid, so you still owe $3: -3.
